lessons.title: Determine Surface Area of Prisms
lessons.objective: I can find the surface area of rectangular and triangular prisms.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words surface area, rectangular prism, triangular prism, and face.

concept.heading: How do we find the surface area of a prism?
concept.intro: Surface area is the total area of all the faces of a solid. A rectangular prism has 6 faces; a triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles). Add every face to get the total.
concept.keyIdea: Surface Area of Prisms. Formula: Surface Area = Sum of areas of all 6 faces. 1. Calculate area of Top & Bottom: 2 × (l · w). 2. Calculate area of Front & Back: 2 × (l · h). 3. Calculate area of Left & Right: 2 × (w · h), then sum all three pairs

worked.title: Watch me
lines: My triangular prism has triangle bases (base 6 in., height 4 in.), is 10 in. long, and the two slant sides are 5 in. each.
Each triangle base is ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, and there are 2 of them: 2 × 12 = 24.
Now the 3 rectangles: 6 × 10 = 60, 5 × 10 = 50, and 5 × 10 = 50, which add to 160.
I add the bases and the rectangles: 24 + 160 = 184.
So the surface area is 184 in². I counted 5 faces because it is a triangular prism.
linesEs: Mi prisma triangular tiene bases triangulares (base 6 pulg, altura 4 pulg), mide 10 pulg de largo, y los dos lados inclinados miden 5 pulg cada uno.
Cada base triangular es ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, y hay 2: 2 × 12 = 24.
Ahora los 3 rectángulos: 6 × 10 = 60, 5 × 10 = 50 y 5 × 10 = 50, que suman 160.
Sumo las bases y los rectángulos: 24 + 160 = 184.
Entonces el área de superficie es 184 pulg². Conté 5 caras porque es un prisma triangular.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a rectangular prism: 5 long, 4 wide, 3 tall. How many faces does it have?
Top and bottom: 5 × 4 = 20, times 2 = 40. Front and back: 5 × 3 = 15, times 2 = 30.
Left and right: 4 × 3 = 12, times 2 = 24. Now add 40 + 30 + 24. What is the surface area?
Yes, SA = 94 cm². Surface area always uses square units.
linesEs: Ahora un prisma rectangular: 5 de largo, 4 de ancho, 3 de alto. ¿Cuántas caras tiene?
Arriba y abajo: 5 × 4 = 20, por 2 = 40. Frente y atrás: 5 × 3 = 15, por 2 = 30.
Izquierda y derecha: 4 × 3 = 12, por 2 = 24. Ahora suma 40 + 30 + 24. ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
Sí, 94 cm². El área de superficie siempre lleva unidades cuadradas.

lessons.title: Determine Surface Area of Pyramids
lessons.objective: I can find the surface area of a pyramid by adding the base area and the lateral faces.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my work using the words pyramid, slant height, lateral face, and base.

concept.heading: How do we find the surface area of a pyramid?
concept.intro: Surface area of a pyramid is the base area plus all the triangular side faces. A square pyramid has 1 square base and 4 triangular faces. Each triangle uses the slant height: ½ × base × slant height.
concept.keyIdea: Surface Area of Pyramids. Formula: Surface Area = Base Area + Sum of Triangular Lateral Faces. 1. Calculate area of base polygon (square, rectangle, or triangle). 2. Calculate area of each triangular face using ½ × base × slant height. 3. Add the base area and all triangular face areas together

worked.title: Watch me
lines: My square pyramid has a 6 in. × 6 in. base and a slant height of 8 in.
Now one triangular face: ½ × 6 × 8 = 24. A square pyramid has 4 of them, so 4 × 24 = 96.
I add the base and the side faces: 36 + 96 = 132.
So the total surface area is 132 in². I used the slant height (8) for the triangles, not the pyramid's height.
linesEs: Mi pirámide cuadrada tiene una base de 6 pulg × 6 pulg y una altura inclinada de 8 pulg.
Primero el área de la base: 6 × 6 = 36.
Ahora una cara triangular: ½ × 6 × 8 = 24. Una pirámide cuadrada tiene 4, así que 4 × 24 = 96.
Sumo la base y las caras laterales: 36 + 96 = 132.
Entonces el área de superficie total es 132 pulg². Usé la altura inclinada (8) para los triángulos, no la altura de la pirámide.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller square pyramid: base 4 × 4, slant height 5. What is the base area?
Right, 4 × 4 = 16. Now one triangular face: ½ × 4 × 5. What do you get?
Yes, 10. Four faces is 4 × 10 = 40. Now add the base: 16 + 40. What is the surface area?
Yes, SA = 56 in². Don't forget to add the base area!
linesEs: Ahora una pirámide cuadrada más pequeña: base 4 × 4, altura inclinada 5. ¿Cuál es el área de la base?
Correcto, 4 × 4 = 16. Ahora una cara triangular: ½ × 4 × 5. ¿Qué obtienes?
Sí, 10. Cuatro caras son 4 × 10 = 40. Ahora suma la base: 16 + 40. ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
Sí, 56 pulg². ¡No olvides sumar el área de la base!

vocabulary.definition: A triangle side of a pyramid, not the bottom.

vocabulary.definition: The flat bottom of a pyramid.

vocabulary.definition: The point at the top of a pyramid where the sides meet.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of just the side triangles, not the bottom.

vocabulary.definition: The total area of every face of a solid, base included.

support.prompt: What is the surface area of a rectangular prism with l = 5 cm, w = 4 cm, h = 3 cm?
feedback: You found half the faces — remember each face has a matching opposite face to double.
That's the volume — surface area adds up all six face areas instead of multiplying three edges.
Check the units — a surface measurement needs square units, not cubic.
hints: You need surface area — the total of all 6 face areas of the 5 × 4 × 3 prism — not the space inside.
Use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh: three different faces, each with a matching twin on the opposite side.
Find the three face areas first: 5×4 = 20, 5×3 = 15, and 4×3 = 12. Double each, then add the results.

support.prompt: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
support.explanation: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangular bases and 3 rectangular lateral faces.
feedback: That's just the rectangular sides — don't forget the two triangular ends.
Count again — a triangular prism has more rectangular sides than that, plus its two ends.
That's the face count for a rectangular prism — a triangular prism has one fewer face.
hints: Picture a tent or a triangular chocolate box: two triangle ends plus rectangles wrapping around the sides.
Count the two triangular bases first, then count one rectangle for each side of the triangle.
A triangle has 3 sides, so count 3 rectangular faces. Then add the triangular ends to that count.

support.prompt: A triangular prism has two triangular bases each with area 12 cm² and three rectangular faces with areas 30 cm², 40 cm², and 40 cm². What is the total surface area?
feedback: You added the three rectangles but left out both triangular bases.
You included only one triangular base — a prism has two matching triangular ends to add.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: All five face areas are given: two triangles of 12 cm² each, and rectangles of 30, 40, and 40 cm².
Total surface area = every face added once — count BOTH triangular bases, not just one.
Start with the triangles: 2 × 12 = 24 cm². Then add the three rectangle areas to that.

support.prompt: Spot the Common Mistake — A Forgotten Face
steps: Dimensions: Rectangular prism time capsule: l = 5 in, w = 3 in, h = 2 in.
Formula: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh (add all 6 faces).
Calculate: The student wrote SA = 2(5×3) + 2(5×2) + (3×2) = 30 + 20 + 6 = 56 in².
support.explanation: The student forgot to multiply the last face pair (3×2) by 2. It should be 2(3×2) = 12, not 6. Correct: SA = 30 + 20 + 12 = 62 in².
hints: A prism has 6 faces, in 3 matching pairs — every pair gets multiplied by 2.
The last term should be 2(3×2) = 12, not 6. Correct SA = 30 + 20 + 12 = 62 in².

support.prompt: A square pyramid has a base edge of 5 in and a slant height of 7 in. What is the surface area?
support.explanation: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². SA = 25 + 70 = 95 in².
feedback: You calculated the four triangular faces but forgot to add the square base area.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
Recheck each triangular face area — make sure you take half of base times slant height for each.
hints: A square pyramid has TWO kinds of faces: one square base (5 × 5) and four identical triangles with slant height 7.
SA = base area + 4 triangle areas, where each triangle is ½ × base edge × slant height.
Base first: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Then one triangle: ½ × 5 × 7. Multiply that by 4 and add the base area.

support.prompt: How many lateral (triangular) faces does a square pyramid have?
support.explanation: A square pyramid has a square base and 4 triangular lateral faces — one for each side of the square.
feedback: A square base has four sides — count a triangular face for each side of the square.
The square base isn't a lateral (triangular) face — only count the slanted triangle sides.
That's too many — count only the slanted triangular sides around the square base.
hints: Lateral faces are the slanted triangles on the sides — the square base itself doesn't count.
Each side of the square base holds up exactly one triangle. Count the sides of a square.
Trace the base: it's a square. Count one triangle leaning against each side of that square.

support.prompt: What is the area of one triangular face with base 8 in and slant height 6 in?
support.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 in².
feedback: Adding the base and height won't give area — multiply them first, then take half.
Check the units — a flat triangular face needs square units, not cubic.
Don't forget to take half — a triangle's area is half of base times height, not the full product.
hints: You have one triangle: base 8 in, slant height 6 in. Triangle area is not just base × height.
Use area = ½ × base × height — multiply the two numbers first, then take half.
Multiply 8 × 6 = 48 first. Then take half of that result.

steps: Box: Square pyramid: base edge = 5 in, slant height = 6 in
One Triangular Face: ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 in²
Four Faces: 4 × 15 = 60 in²
Answer: SA = 60 in² (stopped after the four triangular faces)
support.explanation: The student found the lateral area (60 in²) but forgot to add the base. Base area = 5 × 5 = 25 in². Correct SA = base + lateral = 25 + 60 = 85 in².
hints: Did the student include the bottom of the pyramid?
Surface area = base area + lateral area. Add the base: 25 + 60 = 85 in².

support.prompt: Predict the prism surface area for these settings. Give the answer in square units. Round to four decimal places if needed.
support.explanation: 2(6×4 + 6×5 + 4×5) = 148. The net has three pairs of congruent rectangles. Add the areas of all six faces.

support.prompt: A rectangular prism measures 4 by 3 by 2 units. Find its total surface area.
support.explanation: Three face pairs give 2(4×3 + 4×2 + 3×2) = 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 52 square units.
hints: Name the given quantities and the quantity you need.
Draw a model or write the relationship first. Check your answer in the original situation.

support.prompt: A right square pyramid has base side 6 units and slant height 5 units. Find its total surface area.
support.explanation: The base has area 36. Each triangular face has area 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15. Four triangles plus the base give 60 + 36 = 96 square units.
hints: Name the given quantities and the quantity you need.
Draw a model or write the relationship first. Check your answer in the original situation.

core.prompt: A triangular prism has triangular bases with base 6 in and height 4 in. The prism is 10 in long and the two slant sides of the triangle are each 5 in. What is the surface area?
core.explanation: Triangular bases: 2 × (½ × 6 × 4) = 24 in². Three rectangular faces: 6(10) + 5(10) + 5(10) = 60 + 50 + 50 = 160 in². SA = 24 + 160 = 184 in².
feedback: You added the two slanted rectangular faces and the bases but missed the bottom rectangular face.
You added the three rectangular faces but left out the two triangular bases.
Check the units — a wrapped surface is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: Gather the parts: two triangle bases (base 6 in, height 4 in) and three rectangles, each 10 in long.
SA = 2 triangle areas + 3 rectangle areas. Each rectangle is one triangle side (6, 5, or 5) times the 10 in length.
Triangles first: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, doubled is 24 in². Then find the rectangles: 6 × 10, 5 × 10, and 5 × 10.

core.prompt: Spot the Common Mistake — Surface Area or Volume?
steps: Dimensions: Rectangular prism time capsule: l = 7 in, w = 4 in, h = 3 in. Find the surface area.
Formula: Surface area adds all 6 faces: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh.
Calculate: The student multiplied the three dimensions: 7 × 4 × 3 = 84, so they wrote SA = 84 in².
core.explanation: Multiplying l × w × h gives the VOLUME (84 in³), not surface area. Add all six faces: SA = 2(7×4) + 2(7×3) + 2(4×3) = 56 + 42 + 24 = 122 in².
hints: l × w × h fills the inside (volume, cubic units). Surface area covers the outside.

core.prompt: A square pyramid has a base area of 49 cm² and a total lateral area of 84 cm². What is the surface area?
core.explanation: SA = Base Area + Lateral Area = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².
feedback: That's just the base area — add the lateral (triangular) area too for the total.
That's just the lateral area — add the base area too for total surface area.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: Both pieces are already given: base area 49 cm² and lateral (triangle) area 84 cm².
Total surface area = base area + lateral area — one addition, keeping square units.
Set up the sum 49 + 84 and add carefully, keeping cm² in your answer.

steps: Box: Square pyramid: base edge = 8 in, slant height = 10 in
Base Area: 8 × 8 = 64 in²
One Triangular Face: 8 × 10 = 80 in² (forgot the ½)
core.explanation: A triangle's area is ½ × base × height, so each face is ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², not 80 in². The student left out the ½. Four faces: 4 × 40 = 160 in². Correct SA = 64 + 160 = 224 in².
hints: Look at the triangular-face step — what is the area formula for a triangle?
Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. Each face is ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², so SA = 64 + 4 × 40 = 224 in².

stretch.prompt: Compare two closed containers: a rectangular prism (8 × 6 × 4 in) and a triangular prism whose ends are right triangles with perpendicular legs 6 in and 8 in and hypotenuse 10 in. The triangular prism is 8 in long. Which uses less protective film to cover every face? Show your work.
stretch.frame: Rectangular prism SA = 2(___) + 2(___) + 2(___) = ___ in². Triangular prism SA = 2(___) + ___ + ___ + ___ = ___ in². The ___ uses less film because ___.
stretch.explanation: The rectangular prism has surface area 2(8 × 6) + 2(8 × 4) + 2(6 × 4) = 208 in². The triangular prism has two ends totaling 2(½ × 6 × 8) = 48 in² and three rectangles totaling (6 + 8 + 10) × 8 = 192 in². Its total is 240 in². The rectangular prism uses 32 in² less film.
hints: Both containers get wrapped, so compare SURFACE AREAS. Collect each shape's faces before calculating.
Rect prism: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh. Tri prism: 2 triangle bases + 3 rectangles (each side length × the 8 in length).
Rect prism first: faces are 8×6 = 48, 8×4 = 32, 6×4 = 24. Double each and add, then tackle the triangular prism.

steps: Dimensions: Square pyramid: base edge = 10 in, slant height = 8 in
Base Area: 10 × 10 = 100 in²
Lateral Area: ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in² (one face). Total lateral = 40 × 3 = 120 in²
Answer: SA = 100 + 120 = 220 in²
stretch.explanation: A square pyramid has 4 lateral faces, not 3. Total lateral = 40 × 4 = 160 in². Correct: SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².
hints: Check Step 3: how many lateral faces does a square pyramid have?
A square base has 4 sides, so there are 4 triangular faces. The student only multiplied by 3.

stretch.prompt: Two pyramids have the same base area (64 in²) but different slant heights. Pyramid A has slant height 6 in and Pyramid B has slant height 10 in. How much more surface area does Pyramid B have? Why does slant height affect surface area but NOT base area?
stretch.frame: Pyramid A: SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 6) = 64 + ___ = ___ in². Pyramid B: SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 10) = 64 + ___ = ___ in². Pyramid B has ___ more in² because ___. Slant height only affects ___ because ___.
stretch.explanation: With a 64 in² base the edge is 8 in, so Pyramid A has SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 6) = 64 + 96 = 160 in² and Pyramid B has SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 10) = 64 + 160 = 224 in², a difference of 64 in². Slant height only appears in the triangle formula, so it stretches the lateral faces while the base area stays 8 × 8 no matter how tall the pyramid gets.
hints: Both pyramids share a 64 in² base (edge 8 in). Only the slant heights differ: 6 in versus 10 in.
Find each SA = 64 + 4 × (½ × 8 × slant height), then subtract the totals. The base never uses the slant height.
Pyramid A first: one triangle is ½ × 8 × 6. Multiply by 4, add 64, then repeat using slant height 10.
